datasets.sources: 1-3 explicit canonical single-table query projections with existing read/query grants; no arbitrary joins, SQL or DSL
datasets.authorization: explicit field grants or configured model roles; wildcard field grants cannot open datasets; existing single-table wildcard behavior is unchanged
datasets.numbers: same exactdecimal coefficient arithmetic as transactions; decimalText/integerUnits, scale <= 18 and digits <= 38; sums return fixed-scale strings; unknown/pending/unallocated never become a complete zero
datasets.snapshot: all source schemas, rows, clocks and computed versions are read in one short PocketBase transaction; immutable Host cache is not a second authority
datasets.validation: every page, summary and export rechecks current installation, grant closure and the full version vector in Go; any change is stale, never silently refreshed
datasets.projection: explicit canonical fields; relation IDs require target table/id grants; local formula dependencies require recursive field grants; lookup, cross-table computed paths and computed filters are explicitly unsupported
datasets.computedFields: each source carries canonical computed field IDs derived only from Go schema descriptors; Host forwards this metadata and unwraps only these fields for CSV; ordinary JSON preserves every key even when named fresh/value/state
datasets.budget: SQLite measures only projected cells before driver materialization; all sources share a raw byte budget, then the complete Go JSON envelope including scope, rows, summaries and versions must fit encodedBytes or the open is rejected
datasets.export: CSV from the exact immutable source rows and canonical fields, current authorization and versions rechecked before atomic file commit; existing native file picker and ordinary file authorization apply; no implicit newer query
datasets.lifecycle: opaque surface/workspace/session/installation-bound handle; release, cancel, retirement, expiry and stale authorization reclaim it; SDK pages finally and dispose release ownership; existing bounded subscriptions provide invalidation

dataVersions.request: contract plus 1-64 explicit sources {collection, fields} with canonical field IDs covering the plugin's actual projection; optional versions must echo a prior data.versions response for the same projection. Duplicate JSON members, duplicate collections or fields, unknown or incorrectly cased keys, over-limit batches, relation paths and incomplete or null prior versions reject the whole batch before any read
dataVersions.response: contract, versions keyed by collection with schemaRevision, dataRevision, clockPeriod and computed, and stale (collections whose version differs) only when the request carried versions. The computed map uses projected canonical field IDs, while dataset versions use physical names. Data revisions are non-negative JS-safe integers. Computed fields must be ready with a positive JS-safe definition revision and a nonempty watermark; otherwise the whole batch fails plugin_query_failed. Clock periods come only from clocks referenced by projected computations
dataVersions.snapshot: current installation (action/entry binding, installation revision, model binding diagnostics) and every source's canonical schema/data versions are read in exactly one short PocketBase transaction with one pinned formula evaluation instant and one dependency-graph cache for the whole batch; only metadata is read, never business rows, dataset pages or cursors; unchanged versions cost no extra reads
dataVersions.authorization: every requested source, projected field and same-row formula dependency must hold current read/query grants or the whole batch fails plugin_read_denied. The source grant is checked before existence. Lookups and formulas with unverifiable dependencies such as cross-table expressions fail plugin_query_computed_unsupported
dataVersions.oldHosts: hosts without the method reject it explicitly with plugin_api_unsupported; permission, corruption and identity failures never claim a missing capability and never fall back to another resolution path

dataSnapshot.request: contract plus 1-64 explicit sources {query} where query is the ordinary plugin-query.v2 projection (collection, fields, optional ids, filters, sorts) without cursor or pageSize. Duplicate JSON members, duplicate collections or fields, unknown or incorrectly cased keys, explicit nulls, the mere presence of cursor or pageSize inside a query (the SDK rejects that locally with the same code, before any wire call), $-prefixed collections, over-limit batches and relation paths reject the whole request before any read; the authorization rules are data.query's: projection, sort and filter leaf fields need grants (a filter group is structure, not a read) and ids additionally need the id grant at open and again at every validation
dataSnapshot.response: contract, versions keyed by collection (the exact data.versions vector: schemaRevision, dataRevision, clockPeriod and computed keyed by canonical field ID), binding and sources in request order, each with collection, fields, computedFields, items in data.query row shape, rowGuards as exactly one [id, digest] pair per row aligned with items (null where the id grant did not hold at open, in which case no business record is loaded for a guard that would be discarded; items never carry an unprojected id), filteredRows, totalRows and complete; the Host publishes a handle only for a corpus it can slice that way. binding is Host-only: the audit sequence (positive integer) of the completed model record the corpus was authorized under, fixed inside the open transaction, or null without one; the plugin never sees it and the Host replays it verbatim on every validate
dataSnapshot.snapshot: scope, grants, every source version, projection and row are resolved in one short PocketBase transaction with one pinned formula evaluation instant and one dependency-graph cache; rows come from the same bounded read as datasets and the same row digest as data.query; the transaction closes before the plugin receives the handle and no workspace write transaction is held while paging; digests are attached to a page or corpus all-or-nothing, so a cancelled, deleted or unencodable row never leaves a partially guarded result
dataSnapshot.pages: per source in data.query page shape; pages are slices of the materialized snapshot, so later row writes never mix into an open snapshot and never add rows to it. Data revisions and clock periods are not rechecked while paging; schema revision, installation revision, model binding, session identity and the authorization of every projected, filtered and sorted field are rechecked in Go before every page. The validate request replays the plugin's sources, the version vector and the binding; Go resolves the completed model record again inside the same authorization transaction and a different record (a legitimate remap, even under the same installation and schema revisions with every projection still readable; a record that no longer applies; none versus bound) fails plugin_snapshot_stale, so a handle never survives a change of the binding it was opened under and is never revived by mapping back. A validate request without binding, or with anything but a positive integer or null, fails plugin_capability_invalid before any transaction. Every validate reply must carry an explicit valid true (anything else is plugin_snapshot_stale and drops the handle) plus identity, a per-collection map of whether the plugin may currently read id; rowGuards reach the plugin keyed by row id exactly like data.query (projected or not) only for rows whose source identity is currently true, otherwise {} (string digests, at most one per served row, and whenever id is projected every key is a served row's id); a non-null nextOffset is always below filteredRows and only the final slice of a source carries null; items never gain an unprojected id. After the validate round trip the Host re-checks the handle and its absolute expiry before slicing; a cancellation between that endorsement and the delivery of the slice reclaims the existing handle as well, and the SDK delivers no page or batch that lands after its caller aborted: the handle is released and dropped instead
dataSnapshot.batches: snapshot.readBatch params are {snapshotId, next: {collection, offset} | null}; the reply is {snapshotId, chunks, next, versions} where chunks tile the sources in request order from that position (empty sources as zero-row chunks, each chunk {collection, items, rowGuards, nextOffset, complete}), the whole batch carries at most batchRows rows and batchBytes across source boundaries (only the batch's very first chunk and very first row are unconditional, so a source whose chunk or next row no longer fits starts the following batch as a whole), next is the exact position to pass back or null once every source is exhausted, and the same single Go revalidation as a page precedes every batch. Byte budgets are measured on the form the bridge actually encodes (the default JSON encoder escapes CJK and HTML-sensitive characters to \uXXXX, up to six times their raw JSON size): batchBytes counts everything the batch carries — every chunk's two containers and fixed members, every row's item, served guard and separators; the Host budgets every row plus its guard and the version vector at open (encodedBytes, and each row must fit one reply on its own, else plugin_snapshot_limit), and the whole batch reply (envelope, version vector, items and guards) stays inside the 1 MiB frame. A malformed position fails plugin_capability_invalid (an unknown collection plugin_read_denied) after that revalidation and never drops the handle; the SDK checks the reply fail-closed against its own source list
dataSnapshot.authorization: existing read/query grants with explicit fields only, resolved per concrete source table exactly like ordinary reads (the table's own entries plus $active entries while the table is the active table; requests never send $active): an entry carrying * or $configured is skipped whole and never denies or authorizes a source (a field that only such an entry lists grants nothing), so a wildcard next to explicit grants (the active table being a model table whose manifest grant is $active: *) opens on the explicit grants alone and a wildcard alone fails plugin_read_denied; open, validate, the version vector, same-row formula dependency authorization and row guards all use this one grant while describe/query/versions keep the merged one; an active-table change is re-resolved only when Go receives a different activeCollection (the WPF Host binds activeCollection into the session identity and reports plugin_session_stale first): a projection that then lacks an explicit grant for a used field, including a same-row formula dependency re-authorized on the full closure path, fails plugin_read_denied at open and at validate, while a projection that only loses id keeps validating with valid true and identity false (guards withheld); same-row formula dependencies need recursive grants and lookups or cross-table formulas fail plugin_query_computed_unsupported exactly as data.versions; model output fields follow the current completed model binding; a valid remapping invalidates the previous handle with plugin_snapshot_stale, while an invalid current model binding can fail authority resolution with plugin_model_binding_stale
dataSnapshot.lifecycle: opaque surface/workspace/session/installation-bound handle; release, cancel, retirement, expiry and a failed validation reclaim it; SDK close and dispose release ownership; an expired, released or schema-changed handle is plugin_snapshot_stale and never silently refreshed; the perSurface and total limits count in-flight opens from the moment the Host starts materializing until the handle is published or the open fails, so concurrent opens never build a corpus the Host would refuse to publish, and every admission first sweeps handles whose absolute lifetime ran out instead of waiting for the cleanup timer; before publishing, the Host checks that the validate request of the handle (the plugin's sources, the version vector and the binding) fits the frame under the same encoding as every authority call, so an open whose validate could never be sent fails plugin_snapshot_limit as a whole with its reservation handed back
dataSnapshot.oldHosts: hosts without snapshot methods reject them explicitly with plugin_api_unsupported; permission, corruption and identity failures never claim a missing capability and never fall back to data.query

limits.budgetUnit: UTF-8 bytes of the bridge-encoded reply (default JSON encoder), never raw JSON length; encodedBytes covers items, rowGuards and versions of the whole corpus, batchBytes every chunk (containers and fixed members) and every row (item, guard, separators) of one batch

model.declaration: closed permissions.model logical entities (at most 45) and fields (64 per entity); no arbitrary scripts or SQL
model.outputFile: protected single file, maxBytesPerFile 1..33554432, one exact allowedMimeTypes entry, no thumbs; requires entity update and native archive confirmation; excluded from ordinary model data grants
model.configuration: create/map/repair through native selection and exact confirmation; manual review follows surface lifetime, with bounded authority I/O and commit

catalog.pageBudget: both 32 items and the complete PocketBase HTTP JSON response bytes, including model and continuation; an unrepresentable single item is rejected
catalog.fields: selected tableId plus required schemaRevision, optional offset; identity, label, type, precision and relation endpoints for reviewable suggestions
catalog.validation: current workspace and installation on every page; selected schema revision on every field page

model.authorization: explicit logical-role grants only after complete configuration; current installation rechecked
model.recovery: read/status revalidate completed canonical targets; stale carries logical-path diagnostics and grants no model access; repairs compare the previous binding, history and registered dependencies again in the completion transaction
model.upgrade: additive upgrades of a completed model commit schema and bindings in one workspace transaction; first initialization retains step progress; renames preserve identity, incompatible changes fail closed

transactions.declaration: closed permissions.transactions rules over confirmed model logical entities and fields; unique/reference/conservation/balance/state/sameTarget/groupSameTarget/atMostOne/parentFreeze/reservationBalance/reversalBalance/allocationBalance/settlementBalance/changeEvidence; optional decimal sign/nullable and sameTarget skipEmptyLeftEnd/skipEmptyRightEnd, allocationBalance requireCompleteWhenAllocated with optional parent-relative requireCompleteWhen, settlementBalance scopeDimensions for open reservations and settled actuals, changeEvidence allowInsert, state relationCases; no arbitrary SQL, scripts or unconstrained values
transactions.configuration: transaction.configure registers the manifest declaration after native confirmation; persisted rules survive plugin disable; declaration modelId must equal permissions.model modelId
transactions.numbers: model-bound Text stores canonical fixed-scale decimal text; verified Number fields may use safe integer minor units; shared bounded integer coefficients parse, compare and sum; no float aggregation or implicit rounding
transactions.plan: transaction.preview persists the normalized plan with a stable requestId; the prepared reply carries effects [{tableId, recordId, operation, schemaRevision, expectedDigest? for rows with a before state}], per-table dataRevisions baselines and a monotonic previewRevision >= 1; temporary references bind pre-allocated row ids across tables and one atomic commit
transactions.previewBoundary: preview computes effects and baselines by reusing the Kernel write session on an in-memory record overlay: no PocketBase writes, file hooks, business receipts or publishers; it confirms only the affected boundary and never claims business rules such as balance or conservation pass early
transactions.refresh: explicit {requestId, plan, refresh: true} on transaction.preview reuses the same requestId with an identical plan, keeps newIds, recomputes effects and baselines and increments previewRevision by exactly one; a different plan is input_conflict; requestIds are never rekeyed or auto-refreshed
transactions.submit: public transaction.submit stays {requestId}; the Host takes the current prepared version through native confirmation and forwards its previewRevision to Host-only transaction.commit, which requires previewRevision >= 1 and equal to the persisted prepared revision
transactions.commit: Host-only commit re-verifies, inside the same business transaction, that the actual derived write-set effects and per-table base revisions equal the persisted prepared values; any drift is transaction.plan_stale with zero writes and requires an explicit refresh followed by renewed native confirmation; the persisted applied result keeps newIds and the receipt without effects or baselines
transactions.recovery: transaction.submit consumes one requestId exactly once; missing, stale or epoch-expired ids and unprovable outcomes return unknown; verified success is sticky; never auto-replay, rekey or resubmit

files.ownership: surface, installation id/revision/package, workspace epoch, Host run and purpose

dataIo.tasks: existing HostDataIoTaskRegistry only; scoped handles; status polling
dataIo.import: Python preview, Go plan owner; upsert frozen before native confirmation; canonical single-table mutation <=1000
dataIo.export: explicit fields and authorized query; CSV/XLSX ExportService; raw relation ids only
dataIo.outputReceipt: verified success is sticky; lost receipt is unknown and never replayed
dataIo.files: Host-chosen import/export purpose; same broker; 32 MiB new plugin policy distinct from ordinary 1 MiB
dataIo.importPreview: up to 20 sample rows / 128 KiB; summary covers the complete <=1000-row plan; invalid preview has null planId

attachments.handles: surface-owned opaque references; no raw staged handles, stored names or download tickets
attachments.write: Host-native file selection, staged principal/record/field/file binding, canonical setAttachments and native confirmation
attachments.read: current Go installation and field grant checked for each bounded block
attachments.stageTransport: Host-only attachment.stage JSON envelope <=2 MiB including base64; decoded file <=1 MiB; all other surface HTTP requests <=1 MiB

outputs.source: immutable plugin-declared templateVersion, dataVersion and purpose; not independently verified business facts
outputs.ownership: current surface, installation and workspace; ordinary file and attachment budgets unchanged
outputs.save: native target selection and atomic replacement; stable saveId recovers an in-session receipt; unknown never auto-replays
outputs.archive: existing canonical attachment mutation and native confirmation; immutable artifact source audit in the same business transaction
outputs.reopen: opaque archived artifactId, current installation and canonical field authorization, original issued bytes
outputs.print: opened preview only, never a successful physical printing receipt

ui.transport: trusted parent; existing vibetable.plugin-surface.v1 action service=ui; never a Product RPC
ui.context: presentation only; Go-authorized context.read remains the data authority
ui.tasks: only native tasks owned by the current surface; cancelRequested is not settlement; no confirmation fields

lifecycle.declaration: manifest compatibility.surfaceLifecycle; pluginApi 3.x only; any other value is version_incompatible; a plugin without it keeps the manual entry only

background.mount: hidden isolated frame in the workspace, mounted only while plugin.catalog.list projects surfacePhase background for that very token; never focused, no tab stop, no Product bridge; dropped on workspace switch, disable, uninstall, failure or a lost background grant
background.authority: Host-enforced per surface token before any capability runs; never a renderer flag. The catalog projection is the only trigger for a hidden mount: an application beyond maxBackgroundSurfaces, a Host that omits surfacePhase, or a token that was already promoted keeps its normal manual entry and is never mounted hidden
background.refusal: plugin_surface_background for every other method, including ui tasks.cancel, notification.show and navigation.back
background.dialogs: none; no script dialogs and no modals sandbox flag

lifecycle.catalog: plugin.catalog.list projects action.surfacePhase background only for a token the Host currently grants in background; foreground and ungranted tokens project null, so a consumer that never reads the field behaves exactly as before
lifecycle.promote: only the user opening the entry: the click's plugin.action.describe binds the active collection and promotes the prepared surface token in place, then lifecycleChanged foreground is delivered; the same frame and session become the visible viewport without a reload or a token change
lifecycle.readiness: application readiness is a separate handshake from the transport ready event: a lifecycle-declaring plugin calls api.lifecycle.readyToActivate() once its first view is rendered and it can serve a foreground activation (idempotent, never throws); the frame posts vibetable.plugin-surface.v1 event=readyToActivate payload={} to its parent and the shell consumes it locally (it is never forwarded to the Host authority, whose surface events stay ready | close | action); the SDK posts it only after the Host announced lifecycleChanged, so a Host without this contract never receives it, and an early call is deferred to that first announcement; a pre-warmed frame is reusable only after this signal, a click on a frame without it (still loading, or failed to start) closes it once, and the click's own catalog read opens a fresh surface through the normal visible path; the close always precedes that read so the cold token is never reused; a plugin that never signals is re-opened once per click (bounded, same as the legacy viewport)
lifecycle.demote: leaving the foreground retires the token and releases the frame; a Host never demotes a foreground surface; re-preparing the same entry issues a new background token
lifecycle.rendererRecovery: native stop and renderer recovery retire the old surface tokens before rebuilding. The recovered workspace session projects manual entries with no background phase. An explicit click still opens the application. Opening a new workspace session or starting the application normally allows background preparation
lifecycle.discardedClick: a describe may have promoted its token before the user leaves. The shell closes that token before refreshing the catalog. A newer click on the same entry takes responsibility for that pending token and the older intent cannot affect the replacement. A reply naming a previously replaced token cannot open or close the new frame
lifecycle.applicationOpen: sidebar, toolbar, row context menu and plugin center share the application-open path. Each click has one intent and sends at most one describe. A successful describe promotes its confirmed token in place and the shell adopts that frame without a reload. The active view stays bound to the confirmed installation, revision and token. If the catalog changes that binding, the shell leaves the view and the replacement needs a new click. An install change detected during the click's catalog read ends the old click before it describes any action. A frame that has not signalled readiness closes before the catalog read so the first click can open a fresh visible surface
lifecycle.contextRead: surfacePhase reports the Go-authorized phase of the calling token; a Host without this contract omits it and the SDK reads it as foreground; the SDK phase is monotonic per session, so a late reply or a stale lifecycleChanged never rewinds foreground
lifecycle.transport: trusted parent vibetable.plugin-surface.v1 event=lifecycleChanged payload={phase}; sent before themeChanged on ready and on load, and on every phase change; the SDK ignores a repeated phase and any phase announced after foreground; whenForeground(signal) stops waiting as soon as the signal aborts, even while a context.read is in flight; event=readyToActivate (application readiness, see readiness) is the only other lifecycle event and is consumed by the shell
